subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat `all | final | off` tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config and user-visible failed-mutation delivery semantics; source inspection proves the gap but cannot choose whether UX suppression should override the current safety fallback.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep boolean suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to documentation or channel-specific leak fixes.

options.title: Split by warning family
options.body: Defer a general enum and handle specific remaining leaks, routing needs, or channel aggregates in their own issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged warning-policy work explicitly separated this issue as the broader delivery-policy follow-up.
